Web design McAllen, Texas businesses need has a particular job: catch a shopper who is planning a trip. Someone in Mission, in Weslaco or across the river is deciding where to go this Saturday, what to buy and whether the drive is worth it. If your site shows what you carry, your hours and where to park, you are on the list. If it is a logo and a phone number, you probably are not.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, a Texan building sites by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. You see a free demo of yours before you pay, and the prices are printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

A shopping city whose customers cross a river

McAllen sells far more than its own residents could buy. The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas reported retail sales of $17.5 billion for McAllen in 2023, the highest of any Texas border metro. Its profile of the area has estimated that shoppers from Mexico account for roughly 30 to 40 percent of retail sales, with some driving up from as far as Monterrey. The city's own sales tax take reached a record $96.8 million in 2024, which local officials credited to the two-country economy.

That share is shrinking, though. A January 2026 Dallas Fed study found Mexican shoppers make up a smaller part of Texas border retail than before the 2008 financial crisis, pointing to big-box stores opening in northern Mexico and longer waits at the ports of entry. For a McAllen shop that means the trip has to be worth it, and the website is where a shopper decides.

McAllen web design that treats the Valley as one market

People here cross city lines all day without thinking about it. Federal statistics group McAllen, Edinburg and Mission into one metro area, which was the fifth most populous in Texas at the 2020 count. Pharr, Weslaco, Donna, Alamo and Hidalgo sit along the same stretch of highway. A customer in Edinburg may never type "McAllen" into a search bar, and a plumber based in Pharr may do most of his work in McAllen.

Google ranks local results by relevance, distance and prominence. You cannot move your shop closer to every customer, but you can be clear. A retailer people drive to needs a page that makes the trip easy: address, parking, hours on weekends and holidays, and what is in stock. A service company that goes to the customer needs to name the cities it covers and say something true about each one. Those are two different sites, and we ask which one you are before writing a word.

Two languages, handled honestly

Census Bureau survey figures for 2019 to 2023 show about 73.6% of McAllen residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home. Plenty of customers read both, switch mid-search, or prefer one for certain things. Here is how we plan a site for that without pretending to be something we are not.

  1. Start with the English siteMaurice writes every English page by hand for your business, using your answers about what customers ask most.
  2. Decide which pages need SpanishUsually the home page, services and contact. Not every page needs a twin, and a smaller set of well-written pages beats a full set of rough ones.
  3. Spanish text comes from a fluent writer you trustYou, a relative, a staff member or a paid translator. Dominion does not write Spanish copy, so we will not fake it with a machine.
  4. We build those pages as real pagesEach with its own address and title, linked to its English version, so search engines and customers can find it directly.

Photos you already own beat stock pictures

A shopper deciding whether to drive across town wants to see the actual racks, the actual counter, the actual work. Your phone is good enough. Take a dozen pictures in good daylight: the storefront from the parking lot, the inside from the door, your best sellers, a finished job. We size them so they load fast on a phone. If you sell photography, quinceañera dresses or anything else people judge by eye, a gallery page is worth it, and Pro includes one.

Help for Hidalgo County owners that costs little or nothing

  • UTRGV Small Business Development Center. Part of the South-West Texas Border SBDC Network, it advises businesses in Cameron, Hidalgo, Starr and Willacy counties.
  • McAllen Chamber of Commerce. Its Launch McAllen initiative, built with the City of McAllen and the McAllen Economic Development Corporation, includes IDEAPLACE, a free eight-week program at the McAllen Creative Incubator. The chamber has also run LatinaHope with United Way and Wells Fargo for Spanish-speaking micro-entrepreneurs.
  • McAllen Economic Development Corporation. A nonprofit that works to bring investment and jobs to the region, a partner in the chamber's entrepreneur programs.

How a McAllen owner works with us from East Texas

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in McAllen. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

McAllen is a long drive from Big Sandy, and it does not need to be driven. Questions, photos and page approvals all move by text, email and link.

Common questions

How much does web design in McAllen cost?

Prices in the Valley run from cheap template deals to agency retainers. Ours are fixed and paid once: $497 for a five-page Starter site, $997 for Pro and $1,997 for Agency. After launch, hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent with us. The demo is free, so you know what you are buying before any money changes hands.

Can you write my website in Spanish?

We do not offer Spanish copywriting, and we would rather tell you that now than hand you a machine translation. Maurice writes the English pages. If your customers read Spanish, the Spanish text should come from you, a family member or a translator you trust, and we build it into the site as real pages so Google can read it. We will not put a translate button on and call the job done.

Is a web developer in McAllen, TX the same as a web designer?

Not quite. A designer plans and builds the pages people see; a developer usually writes custom software, such as a booking system or an online store tied to inventory. Most small McAllen businesses need the first. We design, write and build the site and set up the contact forms and the search basics. Online stores and custom software are not part of our packages, and we will say so if that is what you need.

Can one website bring in customers from Edinburg, Mission and Pharr?

It can if you really serve them. Write a short, true section or page about each city you cover, with what you offer there and how far you travel. Pro includes ten city pages written from scratch after research, which fits a service company covering most of Hidalgo County. A storefront that people drive to mostly needs clear directions and hours instead.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
